newsitem.title: USA: Swiss used "Jewish assets" for its own citizens - D'Amato.
newsitem.headline: Swiss used "Jewish assets" for its own citizens - D'Amato.

text.p: The Swiss government, in a secret 1949 deal with Poland, used assets of Polish Jews to compensate Swiss citizens for the nationalisation of their property in the then-Communist country, U.S. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato said on Wednesday.

At an emotional hearing in which Holocaust victims complained of their treatment by Swiss banks, D'Amato said his researchers recently found documents detailing the secret arrangment with Poland and later similar deals with Hungary and Czechoslovakia in U.S. National Archives. He did not make the documents public.
"What we have here is a situation where the Swiss turned over assets that belonged to the Jews of Poland to settle claims made by Swiss citizens," he said after the hearing.

He added that a similar method was used in other East European countries, and named Hungary and Czechoslovakia. He said that Swiss treaties with the East European governments included secret sections on using Jewish assets for compensation in nationalisation claims.

An aide to D'Amato told Reuters that the assets of the Jews that were used to compensate Swiss citizens were on deposit in Switzerland. Neither he nor the senator could give a figure for the amount of compensation involved.

D'Amato is campaigning to force Switzerland to reveal how much money belonging to Holocaust victims and their survivors is in Swiss banks. At the hearing, he charged that newly discovered documents show that Switzerland was a bigger "collaborator" with Nazi Germany that previously imagined.
